## Findings ledger
- [D1.DOC5.F1] Riley uses Weber as a qualified counter-framework to Mann’s account of imperialism: Weber recognizes prestige conflicts but also explains imperialism through material dynamics and political capitalism — dim: place_in_text — text-argument: Riley argues that Mann’s emphasis on militaristic status ideology is inadequate because Weber’s account joins interstate prestige competition to materially driven imperialist expansion — place: adopted analytical counterpoint and qualified framework — anchor: "But Weber’s actual account of imperialism was quite different from Mann’s. It is true that Weber insisted that inter-state competition was saturated with conflicts over prestige." — anchor-b: "Imperialist adventures, investments in arms manufacture, and state loans (phenomena that Weber grouped under the term political capitalism) tended in contrast to have higher rates of return" — doc: em:PSYPHAPS — doc-b: em:PSYPHAPS — confidence: high — trimmed-anchor-b: yes

scope_outcomes.criterion: The citing text must contain a substantive argument that assigns Max Weber an evidentiary, framework, opponent, dialogue, courtesy or qualified role in the text’s argument.
scope_outcomes.basis: The complete supplied text was inspected. Riley explicitly contrasts Weber’s account of imperialism with Mann’s and uses Weber to support a materially grounded interpretation of imperialism alongside prestige competition.
limitations: This outcome concerns only the supplied 2013 text and does not establish Riley’s place for Weber across his complete corpus.
The assessment does not independently verify the cited Weber passages or edition pagination.
